faq: Which payment providers do you work with?

Stripe is our default because its docs and test tools are strong. We can also set up PayPal, Paddle or Lemon Squeezy if they suit your country and product. You need your own account with the provider.
Do I need a business entity to take payments?

Providers set their own rules for who can open an account and where payouts go. We cannot change those rules. Check the provider's requirements for your country before ordering, and we can walk you through the form.
The provider charges fees per payment, billed to your account. Our price covers the setup only. We list the current fee structure in your handover notes so there are no surprises.
Can you move existing customers onto the new billing?
Yes, for a small number of customers by import or manual setup. Large migrations with saved cards need the provider's own migration process, which we can plan but not speed up.

desc:
SaaS payments and subscription billing setup connects your product to a provider such as Stripe, so customers can subscribe or pay once and your app knows who has paid. Ecom Swift LLC builds the checkout, plans, receipts and billing page in your own account.

## What does SaaS payments setup involve?

It means linking three things: a payment provider that holds the money and card details, your product that decides what a customer may use, and the messages between them. When someone pays, the provider notifies your app through a webhook, and your app unlocks the paid features for that account.

Setup also covers the plans themselves: what each costs, how often it renews, whether there is a free trial and what happens when a card fails.

## Why billing is harder than it looks

A Pay button is the easy part. The difficulty comes later: a card expires, a customer upgrades midway through a month, a payment is declined, or a user cancels and expects access to end at the right date. If your app does not hear about these events, paying customers may be locked out while non-paying ones keep using the product.

Handling cards yourself is risky and unnecessary. Hosted checkout keeps card numbers with the provider, which reduces the security burden on a small team and lets customers pay with a trusted page.

## How billing set up properly affects revenue

Revenue depends on the path from interest to payment being short and clear. A hosted checkout with a visible plan, a receipt and a way to manage the subscription removes friction at the moment people are ready to pay. A self-service portal lets customers update a card or cancel without writing to you, which saves support time and avoids payment problems caused by outdated details.

Failed payment handling matters more than most founders expect. Cards fail for ordinary reasons, and a reminder before access ends can recover a customer who never meant to leave. Trials, coupons and yearly plans give you tools to test pricing without rebuilding anything.

## What a complete billing setup includes

- A product and price in your provider account for each plan.
- A hosted checkout page that opens from a button in your app.
- A webhook that updates paid, unpaid and cancelled status in your database.
- Receipts and invoices sent by the provider.
- A customer portal to change cards, switch plans or cancel.
- Handling for failed payments, with retries and notice to the customer.
- Optional free trials and coupon codes.
- Plan limits enforced inside the app, such as seats or projects.
- Sales tax collection configured where it applies.
- A test mode run end to end before any live charge.

## How we set it up

We create the products and prices in your provider account, add a checkout button and write the code that receives payment events securely. We then test the full journey in test mode: sign up, pay, fail a payment, upgrade, cancel. Only after that do we go through a live checklist with you.

The Basic package covers a single plan with hosted checkout and paid status. Standard adds several plans with monthly and yearly options, the customer portal, failed payment handling and a trial. Premium adds plan limits, coupons, tax setup, an invoice history page and a test-and-live checklist. Usage-based billing and a revenue dashboard are available as extras.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Decide your plans and what each includes before building.
- Run every scenario in test mode before accepting real money.
- Keep the provider as the source of truth for payment status.
- Write clear plan names and renewal terms on the pricing page.
- Check that refunds and cancellations behave the way you expect.

**Avoid:**
- Collecting or storing card numbers in your own database.
- Granting access from the checkout button alone without confirming payment.
- Creating many plans before you know what customers choose.
- Hiding renewal dates or cancellation steps.
- Ignoring tax rules where you sell.

## Who this service is for

Founders about to charge for the first time need a reliable path from sign-up to paid account. Products that currently take payment by invoice or bank transfer can move to automated subscriptions. Teams with a basic checkout who lack failed payment handling can add the missing pieces.

## What we need from you

An account with your chosen payment provider, created and owned by you, with us added as a developer or team member where it allows. We also need your plan details and a repository invitation. We never need passwords, and card details never pass through us. Business verification with the provider is completed by you.
